methodological_rigor.justification: This retrospective EHR-based cohort includes a large treated advanced NSCLC population of 910 patients and captures changing first-line treatment patterns from 2014 to 2021 with follow-up through 2022. The design is descriptive rather than causal: it is single-center, excludes trial patients and untreated patients, relies on algorithmic line-of-therapy assignment, and the manuscript states that survival analyses were not adjusted for confounding or tested with multivariable methods. Kaplan-Meier estimates with 95% CIs are appropriate for descriptive OS and rwPFS, but the absence of adjusted comparisons, no imputation except partial dates, and potential misclassification of rwPFS and treatment categories limit statistical inference.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual retrospective cohort study of treated advanced NSCLC patients, giving Oxford LoE 2b. The topic has direct clinical relevance because it evaluates real-world uptake of platinum chemotherapy, ICIs, and targeted therapy, along with OS and rwPFS in a high-mortality oncology population. Relevance is somewhat limited by its descriptive single-center design and lack of adjusted effectiveness analysis, so it supports treatment-landscape understanding rather than changing practice.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE applies to this retrospective cohort, and the manuscript reports data source, eligibility, exclusion criteria, follow-up, treatment categorization, endpoint definitions, masking rules, and ethics approval. It also provides a long and specific limitations section covering single-center scope, trial-patient exclusion, algorithmic treatment classification, rwPFS variability, unadjusted survival analyses, and evolving standards of care. Reporting remains limited by incomplete details in the normalized text on patient-flow counts for each exclusion, and no public data or code repository is described.

novelty_literature.justification: The study is mostly an incremental real-world treatment-pattern and survival description in advanced NSCLC during the immunotherapy era. Similar real-world analyses from multiple countries and the Onco-Optimise platform are cited in the manuscript, limiting originality. Its main distinctive feature is the Italian IRST cohort across 2014-2021, which is useful local evidence but not a novel method, mechanism, or practice-changing finding.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly structured and the abstract concisely summarizes cohort size, treatment shifts, OS, and subgroup trends. Methods are detailed about EHR abstraction, line-of-therapy algorithms, therapy categories, rwPFS definition, date imputation, and data masking. The discussion is balanced and explicitly acknowledges that unadjusted subgroup survival patterns cannot support firm treatment comparisons, although parts of the background and comparative literature discussion are lengthy.

key_strengths: Large real-world advanced NSCLC cohort with 910 treated patients followed across major treatment-era changes.
Captures biomarker testing patterns, first-line treatment shifts, treatment sequencing, OS, and rwPFS.
Manual review and data cleaning were used to improve EHR completeness.
Limitations are unusually explicit about confounding, algorithmic misclassification, rwPFS variability, and COVID-era effects.
key_concerns: Survival analyses are descriptive and not adjusted for confounding, limiting claims about treatment effectiveness.
Single-center treated-only cohort excludes trial participants and untreated patients, creating selection bias.
Line of therapy and treatment intent were algorithmically inferred and may be misclassified.
No dedicated survival analyses for individual EGFR, ALK, or ROS1 alteration groups were conducted.
No public data or code availability is reported.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a useful descriptive real-world NSCLC treatment-pattern study, but the inferential ceiling is limited by unadjusted survival analyses and single-center selection. Tier 3 is plausible, with major revisions needed to tone down effectiveness language or add adjusted analyses.
